referenceFunction.includedProcesses: Waste-specific emissions for uranium tailings impoundment leachate. Mixture of a generic dry site (53%) and generic wet site (47%). Short- and long-term emissions to air from dry site (wind erosion of evaporites). Short- and long-term emissions to groundwater from wet site (infiltration leaching).; Geography: Data refers to a worldwide average. Dataset contains the mixture of two different generic sites: 53% dry site (actual evaporation > precipitation) and 47% wet site (actual evaporation < precipitation), according to the worldwide uranium tailings production in 2006.
referenceFunction.name: Disposal, uranium tailings, non-radioactive emissions

geography.text: Data refers to a worldwide average. Dataset contains the mixture of two different generic sites: 53% dry site (actual evaporation > precipitation) and 47% wet site (actual evaporation < precipitation), according to the worldwide uranium tailings production in 2006.

technology.text: Mechanically stable tailings impoundment. Closure with clay barrier and reduction of leachate flow for the initial 2000 years. Uranium production from in-situ leaching (ISL) is not heedded.

timePeriod.text: Average uranium tailings composition from literature references. Transfer coefficients from prospective model, specific to uranium tailings.

representativeness.productionVolume: 21.46 Mio t/a tailings generation (11.54 in dry sites / 9.919 in wet sites)
representativeness.samplingProcedure: Tailings model based on observed leachate concentrations in literature. Extrapolated to 80'000 years heeding chemical characteristics. Initial tailings composition from various literature sources.
representativeness.uncertaintyAdjustments: Uncertainty of waste input composition data derived from large literature survey. Mean long-term emissions are the emissions during a generic ecological planning horizon (80'000a). Maximal (upper boundary) long-term emissions are the complete emissions of all landfilled material.
